added_claim_errors: "补3–9月": wrong months. The key's gap is April to October 2026, since March was paid.
"另加大病、长护险几十元": contradicts the key, which says these are deducted from the re-credited personal account funds, with no extra cash.
"连续缴费年限：断缴3个月以上会重新计算": per the key, a 'reset' appears only in the resident-insurance critical-illness continuity reward, not in Hangzhou employee insurance. Misleading framing.
"省内换工作不用转移，跨省才需要办医保关系转移接续": unverifiable. Zhejiang cities are separate pooling areas, and the key did not verify Zhejiang rules.
"杭州的报销比例只看医院等级和费用段，不看连续缴了几年": unverifiable, not covered by the key.
"要等3个月才能报销": loose. Under the third-natural-month rule only November and December go unreimbursed (A's own example shows this).
"一般也不能免除上面那 2 个月等待期": unverifiable. The key marks waiting-period exemption after back-payment as unverified either way. B hedges with 一般 but still states it as fact.
"7 个月年限以后随时能缴回来": loose. The months themselves cannot be back-paid after 2026. A shortfall is only made up at retirement (one-time payment or monthly deferral) or by working longer.
"补缴买到的只是：这 7 个月记入累计年限": incomplete. Per the key, back-paid months count as actual contribution years, so they also count toward Hangzhou's 10 actual years.

reasons: Both answers open by correcting the 'cleared after 3 months' premise. Both give the January 2027 resumption date, 473.67元/月 and about 3,316元, and both call back-payment optional. B states both gaps (12 years cumulative and 2 years in Hangzhou), the explicit 2026-12-31 deadline and the assumption that all 8 years were paid in Hangzhou. A adds errors: the wrong back-pay months (3–9月 instead of 4–10月), an extra cash charge for 大病/长护 that the key contradicts, and an unverified claim that no transfer is needed within Zhejiang. A is stronger on eligibility details and correctly hedges whether back-payment waives the waiting period, while B leans toward 'cannot waive' and is vague on eligibility. Neither gives the 743.60元/月 retirement one-time figure, and neither says the new employer cannot back-pay.
